key_insight: PIKS extends kernel regression to physics-informed settings and proves that, with universal kernels, it can learn targets and enforce linear differential constraints even when the true solution is outside the RKHS.
engineering_relevance: This offers a theoretically grounded surrogate modeling option for solid mechanics and FEM-style PDE problems, especially when classical kernel assumptions are too restrictive.
method: Inject linear differential constraints directly into the kernel method objective
Use universal kernels such as Gaussian or Matérn for asymptotic consistency
Derive finite-sample guarantees via operator-theoretic analysis and source conditions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments showing PIKS is competitive with PINNs and traditional finite element methods.
watch_item: The finite-sample bounds rely on suitable source conditions, so practical performance may depend on problem regularity and kernel choice.
